rationale: Start with a broad, moderate-slope scouting gradient at mid temperature to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute while revealing the overall retention window and where the critical adjacent pairs lie.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the objective is now to reduce t_last below 10 min by steepening the gradient while keeping the same composition window and temperature. A moderate step from 20 to 16 min should test time savings with low risk of losing resolution.

Resolution is still comfortably above the 1.5 threshold, so shorten the gradient one more step to try to pull the last peak under 10 min. This directly tests whether we can reach the maximum CRF without yet changing selectivity variables.

We are very close to ideal: the only deficit is one pair slightly below 1.5, while t_last is already under 10 min. Lowering temperature one step may improve selectivity enough to recover that pair while likely keeping the last peak near or below 10 min.

The temperature change hurt selectivity, so return to 40 C and instead slightly narrow the gradient window by lowering phi1 one step. This should flatten the effective slope near the late region and may improve the critical mid-run pair while keeping t_last under 10 min.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the only useful exploitation is to see whether an even shorter run can preserve full resolution. Shortening tG by one step tests the boundary while keeping the successful composition window and temperature unchanged.

At 14 min we have margin on the critical pair, so lower phi1 one more step to see if the narrower window can keep or improve resolution while pulling the last peak just under 10 min. This explores whether a neighboring maximum-CRF method exists with a bit more robustness than the current optimum.

The best method is on a narrow optimum, so probe the opposite temperature direction from the failed 35 C test. Raising T one step may preserve the critical pair while moving the last peak slightly earlier, potentially giving a more comfortable full-credit method.

The optimum appears highly sensitive in selectivity but not strongly in total time, so test a lower starting organic fraction while keeping the successful endpoint, slope, and temperature. Changing phi0 may alter the crowded mid-run spacing enough to improve robustness around the critical pair while staying near the same elution window.

A lower phi0 kept resolution but pushed the run slightly later, so test the opposite direction. Increasing phi0 may move the window earlier while retaining enough selectivity to keep the critical pair above 1.5, potentially yielding another full-credit or near-full-credit method.

The move to higher phi0 improved the full-credit method by shifting the chromatogram earlier while preserving the critical pair, so test one more step upward. This checks whether we can gain additional robustness in run time without letting the 6/7 pair fall below 1.5.

phi0 = 0.15 gives a full-credit method with slightly earlier elution than phi0 = 0.10, so now test whether a higher temperature can shorten retention further without collapsing the critical 6/7 pair. This maps robustness around the newer optimum rather than the already poor 0.10/0.85/45 condition.

Temperature increases strongly damage the critical pair, so return to 40 C and probe endpoint composition instead. Raising phi1 from 0.85 to 0.90 at the successful phi0 = 0.15 tests whether the run can be made slightly faster while still keeping the 6/7 pair above 1.5.

At phi0 = 0.15, increasing phi1 hurt the critical pair but sped up the run, so test the opposite endpoint change. Lowering phi1 to 0.80 may improve the 6/7 resolution margin while showing whether the time penalty is still compatible with a full-credit method.

The 0.15/0.80/14/40 method has comfortable resolution margin but only a slight time penalty, so shorten tG one step to try to bring t_last under 10 min while preserving full resolution. This is the most direct route to another 1.000 method in the nearby design space.

The best full-credit methods are around phi0 = 0.10–0.15 and phi1 = 0.85 at 40 C, but temperature sensitivity has only been tested at phi0 = 0.10 or upward at 45 C. A one-step decrease to 35 C at the current optimum will check whether this region gains selectivity enough to improve robustness while still keeping t_last under 10 min.

Both 35 C and 45 C worsened selectivity near the optimum, suggesting 40 C may be close to a local maximum, but a lower temperature could still reveal a different selectivity regime. Testing 30 C at the proven 0.10/0.85/14 composition window checks for an alternative full-credit method with improved robustness of the critical pair.

With two distinct 1.000 methods already found, use the remaining budget to map a more robust operating point around the better one at phi0 = 0.15. Lengthening tG one step should increase the critical-pair margin above 1.58 while likely remaining under or near the 10 min limit, potentially identifying a safer full-credit condition.

All evidence points to a sharp selectivity optimum near 40 C, but the 45 C test was severe enough that one more step upward can help define the temperature-response shape around the critical pair. This is a final robustness-mapping run near the best composition window without repeating a method.

The best methods sit on either side of the 6/7 resolution threshold, and the 0.10/0.90/14/40 run was only slightly short of full resolution while already under 10 min. Shortening that higher-endpoint method to 12 min tests whether its selectivity pattern differs enough from the 0.85 endpoint family to reveal a distinct high-speed neighborhood.

The remaining unexplored corner near the best conditions is lower phi0 with the higher endpoint at the same 14 min slope and 40 C. This will clarify whether the two full-credit optima are part of a broader ridge in phi0/phi1 space or just isolated points.

With only a few injections left, complete the phi0 = 0.05 slice by testing the lower endpoint. This will show whether reduced phi1 can recover the 6/7 resolution margin enough to offset the likely time penalty and possibly uncover another full-credit method.

With the optimum already found, use the final few injections to map one remaining nearby point combining the shorter 12 min gradient with lower temperature at phi0 = 0.15. This tests whether extra selectivity from cooler conditions can rescue the faster run, which would define the local tradeoff surface around the best method.

One remaining unexplored combination near the known optimum is a slightly longer gradient paired with higher temperature. This checks whether added gradient time can compensate for the strong selectivity loss at elevated temperature and helps complete the local response map before the final injection.

For the final shot, explore one last untested neighbor of the full-credit 0.10/0.85/14/40 method by lowering phi1 another step. This tests whether the endpoint optimum is broad on the low-phi1 side or whether the known 1.000 method is truly isolated.
